system.summary: Confederate Vigenere with selected words enciphered using COME RETRIBUTION, COMPLETE VICTORY, or THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; the key advances over cipher letters only.
system.sibling_key: COME RETRIBUTION fits March–April passages; COMPLETE VICTORY encrypts the two 9 March orders introducing that key; THE NAVY OUR PRIDE is recovered from 9 January external plaintext. Key use varies by recipient.
system.notes: Distinct symbols: the 26-letter alphabet of the tabula recta. The clerks' capitals mislead in a few recurring ways (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, a U-like glyph for IC); every correction is a single glyph and is listed in alignment.tsv.

prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2. Further prior plaintext: OR I/45/2 p.772 (9 January), I/49/2 pp.1223 and1255 (10 and20 April), and an undated pencil interlinear decipherment over the 9 March Wirt Adams order.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded. Bryan Payne (bdpayne) selected catalogue 681, directed the continuation and authorized submission; transcription, analysis and writing by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6), no subagents or independent human reading review claimed.
tools: NARA images and catalog OCR; Internet Archive Official Records OCR

solution.what: Fetched the NARA catalogue records of vols. 196, 11 and 10 and the full-resolution frames listed in the catalogue's OCR run lists; screened them on montages. Vol. 196 frame 0027 has no cipher words (an OCR false hit).
Read the cipher words of vol. 196 fr. 0061 (180 letters) and vol. 11 frs. 0022, 0036 and 0039 (52, 56 and 61 letters) and the clear text around them from the images.

Applied the known Confederate key COMERETRIBUTION, over the cipher letters only, offset 0 at each telegram: English from the first letter in all four telegrams (171/180, 50/52, 46/57, 59/61 letters right as read).

Explained the remaining letters as single misleading glyphs of the clerks' capitals (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, U-like glyph for IC); no correction needs more than one glyph.

Controls on the letters as read (decrypt.py --controls): COMERETRIBUTION offset 0 chi2 19-37; best other offset 92-676; COMPLETEVICTORY 132-381; MANCHESTERBLUFF 133-1072; 200 random keys minimum 75-402; shuffled cipher words with the right key 3-10 letters agreeing on average.

OCR full text of OR Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 searched for each plaintext phrase: the 6 April telegram to Levy is printed in clear on p. 1209. The 12 and 30 March and 8 April telegrams not found in this first search.

Second, independent agent: re-read all four telegrams on its own crops, decrypted them with its own code (same plaintext, 171/180, 50/52, 59/61 letters right as read), corrected the 12 March letter count to 180, read the 8 April date line, and found that the 8 April telegram is printed in clear in OR I/49/2 p. 1216 (the first search missed it because of double spaces in the OCR text). Searched OR I/49 pt. 1 for the 12 March telegram: not found.
The four telegrams written as sentences (<doc>_reading.md). One hole: [?west] in the 12 March telegram, where the cipher gives WEST and the sense wants 'what'.
Located three additional telegrams in OR I/45/2 p.772 and I/49/2 pp.1223,1255; no complete counterpart verified for 18 January. Search failures and limits in WORKLOG.md.
Matched 9 January ciphertext against OR plaintext to infer THE NAVY OUR PRIDE; 86/94 candidate letters agree. Retrospective partition check is not an independent blind holdout.
Transcribed six continuation telegrams; all candidate glyphs remain distinct from reconstructed cipher letters. Retained partial 18 January and unresolved April passages.

Verified two orders dated 9 March to Wirt Adams and D.W. Adams introducing COME RETRIBUTION after this date under COMPLETE VICTORY; 46/47 candidate letters each agree. Wirt copy has complete pencilled decipherment, date/hand unknown.
Replayed alignments; tested alternative known keys/all offsets, 1000 random keys for 9 January, and arithmetic round-trip. No ciphertext-only solver or independent holdout claim.
Added five externally/adjacently supported full readings and one provisional 18 January reading. Partial 8 March Brent fragments support earlier key use in another channel; no full transcript claim.
Refreshed community status: PR186 merged, no later target changes or new comments on PR111/186 found during research.
Six new/improved candidate streams,681 raw letters; line-split STR/ONG restores continuous8March alignment. Glyph uncertainties preserved.
4February Navy telegram fits COME RETRIBUTION;21February Wirt Adams uses COMPLETE VICTORY; recipient-specific chronology, not general first-use claim.
Located existing OR texts:4February I/49/1p955,8April I/49/2p1216,20April p1255. Additional pointers15January I/45/2p785 and13/14February I/49/1pp978–979; bounded searches did not resolve18January.
20April equipment alignment excludes clear of any;8April manuscript TOWARDS differs from printed TOWARD. Danville segmentation remains uncertain.10February Beauregard still decoded not read.
April10 FX/EVWJ may span a line as one word; trial STORES does not resolve final group. No guessed ending accepted.
No reliable April11 plaintext from known-key trials or hill-climbing Vigenere lengths2–24 using shared en-modern fourgrams; transcription unreliable. No new-key conclusion.
Same112-letter experiment recovers COME RETRIBUTION at0% and5% nominal noise, fails at15%; real optimized outputs rejected as incoherent.
Reproduced all six alignments and source references; raw681/reconstructed682 letters, explicit Danville length mismatch; word shares measured separately.

Follow-up CI required reading_review on four inherited and three new partial texts. Read their supplied prose/alignment; added explicitly labelled model reviews without changing word shares, uncertainty marks or prior attribution. Not independent transcription.

outcome.method_basis: The key COMERETRIBUTION was already identified for this correspondence: catalogue entry 681 had read frame 0061 and the vol. 11 OCR runs with it, and it is the known key of Confederate telegraph traffic in 1864-65. It was applied to each telegram from its first cipher letter, word by word; two of the four telegrams are printed in clear in OR I/49/2. Continuation adds known-key readings, existing printed/adjacent decipherments, and the 9 January key inferred from external plaintext; methods distinguished per document.
outcome.notes: Original four telegrams plus five continuation telegrams have full readings; 18 January remains provisional (decoded, not read). Dated local keyword orders on 9 March do not establish a simultaneous global switch. Overall fraction unknown because remaining passages are not exhaustively inventoried. See REPORT-2026-10-28.md and WORKLOG.md for bounded scope and prior print. November continuation: six further candidate alignments and two source pointers, with uncertainties and rejected solver outputs. See REPORT-2026-11-01.md; no full-collection or novel-plaintext claim.

texts.label: Taylor (W. F. Bullock Jr.) to Maury, Meridian, 12 Mar 1865, vol. 196 fr. 0061
texts.summary: At the start of Canby's campaign against Mobile, Taylor asks Maury to report in cipher the cavalry on each side of Mobile Bay, its strength and commander, to keep the cavalry close to the enemy and in telegraphic touch with D. W. Adams and headquarters, and to name a point outside the city for a courier line.
texts.note: read_share from research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: 1 hole in 89 words.

reading_review.by: OpenAI Codex, model review of supplied prose/alignment; not independent transcription
reading_review.note: Coherent cavalry, communications and courier instructions. Existing [?west] and SO wording doubts preserved; this reviews supplied prose/alignment, not a fresh independent image transcription. Independent maintainer review pending.

texts.label: Surget to Taylor, Meridian, 30 Mar 1865, vol. 11 fr. 0022
texts.summary: Surget reports to Taylor the forwarding of Lee's and Pillow's despatches, a (false) report that Sherman had been wounded, and the permission for Federal ambulances between Big Black and Jackson; in cipher he asks that the War Department again be urged to relieve Col. Watts (probably N. G. Watts, the agent of exchange), whose habits unfit him for the position.
texts.note: read_share from research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: no holes in 102 words.

reading_review.by: OpenAI Codex, model review of supplied prose/alignment; not independent transcription
reading_review.note: Coherent report and request to relieve Colonel Watts; cipher sentence about habits reads in context. Identity speculation remains in original notes; no new historical identification. Independent maintainer review pending.
